*Source: [Polished Commander & Warleader](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585170/diamond-polished-spheres-commander-and-warleader-sphere)*

The commander is a martial class built around supporting and coordinating their allies as a battlefield leader, primarily through the Warleader sphere. Commanders learn and master coordination, logistics, and tactics to help both on and off the battlefield, such as to navigate harsh terrains, procure resources, and serve as a representative and diplomat with enemy forces.

**Starting Wealth:** 5d6 x 10 gp (average 175 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

**Starting Age:** Self-taught

**Role:** Commanders are leaders who inspire and coordinate their allies, exhorting them to greater achievements.

**Alignment:** Commanders can be of any alignment, but are typically lawful as their use of tactics and coordination favor an ordered mind.

**Hit Die:** d8

**Class Skills:** The commander’s class skills are Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Handle Animal (Cha), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (engineering) (Int), Knowledge (geography) (Int), Knowledge (history) (Int), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

**Skill Ranks Per Level:** 6 + Int modifier.

**Proficiencies:** Commanders receive a martial tradition, gaining proficiency with simple weapons, light armor, and bucklers, in addition to the combat talents granted by their martial tradition.

# Class Features

The following are class features of the commander class:

## Combat Training

Commanders are considered adept practitioners and gain combat spheres and talents according to **Table: Commander**.

## Battlefield Operator

At 1st level, a commander gains the Warleader sphere as a bonus sphere, plus an additional Warleader sphere talent at each odd level after 1st.

## Lingering Commands (Ex)

*A commander’s presence lingers in the minds of their soldiers, guiding them for longer.*

At 1st level, the commander increases the duration of their Warleader sphere abilities by 1 round, +1 round at 4th level and every 3 commander levels thereafter.

Instantaneous and permanent effects are unaffected by this ability.

## Decorum (Ex)

At 2nd level, the commander gains a bonus to Diplomacy, Intimidate, and Profession (soldier) equal to 1 + 1 per 2 class levels (+2 at 2nd level).

At 7th level, the commander gains a +1 bonus to the saving throw DCs of the Warleader sphere and of any combat sphere whose associated skill is Diplomacy, Intimidate, or Profession (soldier), increasing by an additional +1 at 12th and every 5 levels thereafter.

**Veteran’s Welcome:** At 12th level, the commander is known and respected as a military tactician and veteran of many combats. Military organizations (armies, mercenary bands, navies, and so on) are treated as friendly to the commander, even if that organization is allied with a government or group that is hostile to the commander. This allows the commander to gain access to a military encampment, fortress, stronghold, or other location, so long as it is on peaceful terms.

**Respected Legend:** At 17th level, the commander’s reputation has outgrown any single army or nation. Any military organization, regardless of allegiance or hostility toward the commander’s own affiliations, will grant the commander a private audience with their leadership upon request and will not attack the commander on sight solely due to political affiliation (unless the commander’s individual actions or conduct later provokes hostility).

**Special - *Spheres of Guile*:** If you are using *Spheres of Guile*, the decorum class feature’s saving throw DC increase also applies to skill spheres.

## Enhanced Tactic (Ex)

*Each commander takes to the field differently, leveraging their hard-won experience or learned knowledge.*

At 2nd level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the commander gains an enhanced tactic.

Rules and a list of enhanced tactics are included here.

## Battlefield Specialty (Ex)

*Preferences are kind, but the best learn to mitigate what they dislike. The commander develops methods and means to leverage the terrain to their best advantage.*

At 3rd level, and every 6 levels thereafter, the commander gains a battlefield specialty.

Rules and a list of battlefield specialties are included here.

## Commander’s Inspiration (Ex)

At 5th level, an ally benefitting from the commander’s Warleader sphere effects also gains a +1 circumstance bonus to their attack rolls and damage rolls, increasing by +1 every 6 levels after 5th.

## Logistics Specialty (Ex)

*A commander’s greatest victories are often won before the first blade is drawn. Their supply lines secured, their contacts known, and contingencies readied.*

At 7th level, and every 6 levels thereafter, the commander gains a logistics specialty,

Rules and a list of logistics specialties are included here.

## Seize the Moment (Ex)

At 10th level, the commander gains *seize the moment*, a Warleader sphere ability.

### Seize the Moment

**Descriptor:** auditory (voice) and/or visual
**Action:** standard action
**Range:** personal
**Duration:** until the end of the commander’s next turn.
**Target / Area:** the commander and all allies who can see or hear the commander

**Effect:** All allies regain martial focus (if they can maintain martial focus). For the duration, allies gain a +4 morale bonus to all attack rolls, damage rolls, saving throws, AC, and CMD, increasing by +1 every 5 levels after 10th.

*Seize the Moment* may only be used once per combat and its duration cannot be extended by any other effect.

## Never Falter (Ex)

*Your ranks have never broken, even in the face of a tide of horrors.*

At 11th level, the commander becomes immune to fear. Allies benefitting from the commander’s Warleader sphere effects instead gain a +4 morale bonus on saving throws against fear effects.

If one of the commander’s allies would become frightened or panicked (and forced to flee from the source of their fear), that ally can choose to instead move to place themselves nearby the commander (for the purposes of this ability, “nearby” is 15 feet, +5 feet per 5 commander levels after 10th) (the ally moves to the best of their ability if unable to move to have the commander nearby). While the commander is nearby, a frightened ally may continue to fight normally (penalized by the frightened condition as normal) while a panicked ally may defend themselves as though they were frightened (instead of being unable to take any actions).

## Major General (Ex)

At 15th level, after initiative is rolled, the commander may either *engage tactics* or *shout* as a free action. If the commander could not take actions during the first round of combat (such as being unable to act during a surprise round), the commander may instead use this ability on the first round they could act. In addition, when leading an army, the commander may choose to grant that army a circumstance bonus equal to their practitioner modifier divided between the army’s DV or OV (such as a modifier of 6 being +6 DV, +4 DV +2 OV, and so on). The commander chooses how to divide this bonus at the start of each turn. See *Ultimate Campaign*, Mass Combat for more details.

## Lord Commander (Ex)

*Countless battles have cemented the commander’s legacy of tactical superiority.*

At 20th level, once per round, after a roll is made but before the results are revealed, the commander or a single ally benefitting from the commander’s Warleader sphere effects may replace their d20 roll with 1 + the commander’s practitioner modifier (as though their natural die roll were 1 + the commander’s practitioner modifier). In addition, the commander’s tactical prowess thwarts the tactics and teamwork of inferior foes. Enemies whose CR is less than the commander’s level do not benefit from positioning (such as flanking, high ground, or cover (excluding total cover)) or teamwork feats against the commander or their allies benefitting from the commander’s Warleader sphere effects.

# Enhanced Tactics

Enhanced tactics are unique abilities and benefits that grant a commander additional tools to coordinate their allies.

Using or activating an enhanced tactic requires no additional actions from the commander unless otherwise stated. Unless otherwise stated, an enhanced tactic is an extraordinary ability, may only be selected once, and has a saving throw DC of 10 + 1/2 the commander’s level + the commander’s practitioner modifier.

If an enhanced tactic grants a benefit to another ally, that ally must be benefitting from one of the commander’s Warleader sphere effects. If an enhanced tactic allows the commander to spend one of their actions to use, the commander must be able to take actions normally (such as not being paralyzed, stunned, or unconscious).

**Granting Actions:** If an enhanced tactic “**grants**” another ally an action, they may do so when that action is granted (as though taking a nonaction, allowing such actions to be taken even when it is not their turn). An ally must take the granted action when it is granted; if the ally does not, the action is lost. An ally must be able to see or hear the commander to be granted an action this way.

**Martial Focus and Enhanced Tactics:** Similar to a sphere ability, enhanced tactics may allow a commander to expend their martial focus to improve that enhanced tactic’s effects.

**Enhanced Tactic Tags:** Certain commander enhanced tactics possess tags, which carry additional rules:

- **[duty]** enhanced tactics allow the commander to respond to the battlefield by providing certain special bonuses or actions. The commander may only use a single [duty] enhanced tactic each round.

#### Command Attack

*The commander calls out to strike.*

The commander gains the following abilities

- **Coordinated Strike:** As a move or swift action after succeeding on an attack action, all other allies threatening the struck target may spend an immediate action to make a single melee attack against the struck target.
- **Soldier, Strike!:** As a standard action, the commander grants another ally a standard action to perform an attack action or perform a combat maneuver.

#### Coordinated Specialist

**Prerequisite:** commander 8th level; command attack, command movement, or command strategy enhanced tactic.

The commander gains the following options based on other enhanced tactics they possess:

- **Command Attack:** Whenever the commander uses coordinated strike, allies may make their attacks as an attack of opportunity (instead of spending an immediate action).
- **Command Movement:** Whenever the commander uses coordinated movement, instead of designating a square, allies may move to be within the threatened area of another ally.
- **Command Strategy:** Whenever the commander uses coordinated adjustment, each ally may perform 1 additional adjustment.

#### Command Attack, Improved

**Prerequisite:** commander 6th level, command attack enhanced tactic.

The commander gains the following abilities

- **Coordinated Volley:** When using command attack’s coordinated strike, instead of only granting an attack to allies threatening the struck target, allies may make either a melee or ranged attack.
- **Soldier, Charge!:** As a standard action, the commander grants another ally a standard action to charge. An ally granted a charge attack this way may move through allied spaces and, if their movement would end in an ally’s space, those two allies may switch spaces during the charging ally’s movement (as though making a 5 foot step). If the ally is mounted, they may perform a mounted charge.

  A charge attack performed this way cannot be combined with the pounce ability, or any other abilities that allow a creature to attack multiple times when they would charge, and cannot benefit from abilities that multiply damage on a charge attack (such as the Spirited Charge feat).

  At 10th level, the commander may use this ability as a swift action after succeeding on a charge attack.

#### Command Movement

*The commander calls out to reposition.*

The commander gains the following abilities

- **Coordinated Movement:** As a move action, the commander designates a square within their *tactic*. All other allies may move up to half their speed directly towards the designated square (or as close as possible). If the commander does not have an active *tactic*, the commander’s space is treated as the designated square.
  - **Augment 1 mf:** Allies may move up to the commander’s base speed (even if greater than their own). If an ally’s movement made this way is greater than their normal speed, they subtract any movement greater than their normal speed from their movement made on their next turn (such an ally moving the commander’s 30 feet, despite only have 20 feet of movement normally, would mean that ally would subtract 10 feet of movement from their next turn; this movement speed reduction can reach 0 for their turn).
- **Soldier, Move!:** As a move action, the commander grants another ally a move action to move.

#### Command Strategy

*The commander calls out to use better strategy.*

**Prerequisite:** commander 6th level.

The commander gains the following abilities

- **Coordinated Adjustment:** As a move action, the commander grants any number of allies the ability to perform an adjustment. Each ally may choose to perform a different adjustment, chosen between: (1) move up to 10 feet; (2) stand up from prone; and (3) retrieve an item or piece of equipment, or an unattended item within their reach. If the retrieved item could be consumed, that ally may spend an immediate action to drink, eat, or otherwise use the item (such as using a potion, alchemical remedy, and so on).
  - **Augment 1 mf:** Adjustments do not provoke attacks of opportunity.
- **Mage, Cast!:** As a standard action, the command grants another ally a standard action to cast a spell, activate a spell-like ability or supernatural ability, or use a magic item (such as using a scroll, wand, or other use-activated wondrous item).

#### Constant Orders

**Prerequisites:** commander 12th level; enhanced tactic that grants actions.

Each round, the commander gains a bonus move or swift action which may only be spent on an enhanced tactic that grants actions to another ally (such as coordinated strike or soldier, move!, but not the soldier, charge! ability unless using that ability’s 10th level upgrade to grant another ally a charge attack after the commander charges).

#### Counterstratagem

The commander gains the Boxing sphere as a bonus sphere.

The commander can ready a *counterpunch* 1 step faster as a “counterstratagem”. When a counterstratagem’s triggers are met, the commander must grant their *counterpunch* to another ally benefitting from their Warleader sphere effects. That ally may benefit from any number of the commander’s Boxing sphere talents to complete the *counterpunch*.

#### Duty of Cunning [Duty]

Once per round, when an enemy’s attack roll misses an ally, that ally can move 5 feet. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity from the attacking enemy.

- **Augment 1 mf:** Until the start of the ally’s next turn, they may move 5 feet (as though being targeted by this enhanced tactic) each time an attack misses them.

#### Duty of Prescience [Duty]

Once per encounter, when an enemy hits an ally or an ally fails a saving throw from a hostile effect, the commander may grant that ally a bonus to their AC or saving throw equal to 1 + the commander’s practitioner modifier (maximum bonus granted equal to the commander’s class level). This bonus can retroactively cause an attack to miss or a saving throw to succeed.

- **Augment 1 mf:** The granted bonus is halved. This augment does not count against this enhanced tactic’s once per encounter limitation.

#### Duty of Valor [Duty]

When an ally takes damage and has their hit points drop below half their total hit points, the commander grants that ally a number of temporary hit points equal to the commander’s class level + the commander’s practitioner modifier. Temporary hit points granted this way last until the end of the target’s next turn. Each ally may benefit from this enhanced tactic once per encounter. At 10th level, and every 10 levels thereafter, the number of temporary hit points granted this way are doubled (2x, 3x, and so on).

- **Augment 1 mf:** These temporary hit points are granted to the target ally before they take the triggering damage.

#### Endless Preparations

**Prerequisite:** commander 12th level.

The commander gains a single Warleader (shout) or (tactic) talent as a bonus talent. Whenever the commander rolls for initiative, they may immediately retrain this talent.

#### Expert Coordinator

The commander gains a teamwork feat as a bonus feat.

The commander shares 1 teamwork feat they know with all allies, even if they do not meet the feat’s prerequisites, +1 additional teamwork feat per 5 commander levels. The commander may change the chosen shared teamwork feats once per round at the start of their turn.

**Special:** A commander may select this enhanced tactic multiple times; each time they do, the commander gains another teamwork feat.

#### Fading Fire

Whenever an ally takes the withdraw action, the commander may allow that ally to make a single weapon attack at their full base attack bonus at any point during their movement (provided the attack is made against a creature they were previously threatened by or are moving away from). The commander may grant an attack this way once each round, +1 additional time per 5 commander levels.

- **Augment 1 mf (special, see text):** An ally may expend their own martial focus to benefit from this enhanced tactic without it counting against the commander’s usage limit per round.

#### General’s Steed

The commander gains the cavalier’s mount class feature, treating their commander level as their effective cavalier level when determining their mount’s statistics. If the commander possesses the casting class feature, the commander’s mount does not lose the share spells ability.

The commander is treated as possessing the Beastmastery sphere’s (ride) package and may select talents with the (ride) tag without needing the base sphere. Animal allies (including the commander’s mount) may benefit from the commander’s Warleader sphere effects and other commander class features without needing to be pushed or handled, and without needing to be taught a trick (such as not needing a trick to benefit from and use the safeguarding measures (tactic) to roll a saving throw twice).

#### Improved Duty

**Prerequisites:** commander 6th level; any [duty] enhanced tactic

Each [duty] enhanced tactic gains the following additional effects:

- **Duty of Cunning (Flanking Gambit):** For 1 round after benefitting from duty of cunning, the benefitting ally may flank the enemy whose attack missed when threatening with another ally (regardless of their positioning) and increases the bonus granted by flanking by an additional +2.
- **Duty of Prescience (Turnabout):** When duty of prescience causes an attack to miss or a saving throw to succeed, the benefiting ally can make a single melee or ranged attack against the source of that attack or effect.
- **Duty of Valor (Battle Fury):** An ally with temporary hit points granted by duty of valor also gains a +2 bonus on attack and damage rolls and a +4 bonus on saving throws against fear effects.

#### Mountaineering

*The commander grants quick instructions to assist in climbing over various obstacles, including calling out handholds, footholds, and piton locations.*

All allies gain a climb speed equal to 5 feet, +5 x the commander’s practitioner modifier. Allies that already possess a greater climb speed instead increase their existing climb speed by half this amount (minimum 5).

All allies may reduce the effective height of any fall by 5 feet, +5 x the commander’s practitioner modifier. This reduction is before attempting an Acrobatics check as part of willingly falling.

**Example:** A commander with a practitioner modifier of 3 would allow allies to treat any fall as 20 feet shorter. This means any fall less than 20 feet would not inflict falling damage. A 30 foot fall would still allow an ally to make a DC 15 Acrobatics check to treat the fall as 10 feet shorter (plus this enhanced tactic’s reduction) to suffer no damage. A 40 foot fall would still inflict 1d6 falling damage even with a successful DC 15 Acrobatics check.

#### Positioning Superiority

**Prerequisites:** commander 6th level.

Allies increase the AC and Reflex saving throw bonus granted by cover by +1, +1 per 10 commander levels.

Allies increase the miss chance granted by concealment by +5%, +5% per 10 commander levels (to a maximum miss chance of 50%).

Whenever the commander uses an enhanced tactic that would grant an ally movement (such as the command movement enhanced tactic), if that ally’s movement causes them to enter cover or concealment (where they previously were not benefitting from cover or concealment), this enhanced tactic’s benefits are doubled for that ally until the start of that ally’s next turn (i.e. doubling the improvement to cover or additional miss chance).

#### Reckless Gambit

**Prerequisite:** commander 8th level.

Each ally may, once per encounter, declare a reckless gambit at the start of their turn before taking any other actions. A reckless gambit must identify a specific course of actions they intend to take during that turn, subject to GM discretion (such as “I will charge and strike that dragon” or “I will escape this grapple” or “my fire will scorch that demon”, representing a charge attempt, an attempt to break a grapple, and an attempt to cast an offensive spell).

During the turn an ally declares a reckless gambit, as a free action, they may gain a luck bonus to a single d20 roll made to accomplish their declared gambit equal to 1 + 1/2 the commander’s practitioner modifier. If that d20 roll fails, that ally suffers a -2 penalty to all d20 rolls until the end of their next turn.

**Example:** An ally declares “I will leap across that chasm, charge the dragon and evade their talons, strike them with my blade and knock them down”. That ally could then, during their turn, gain a luck bonus on their choice of their Acrobatics check to jump across the chasm, their Acrobatics check to avoid an attack of opportunity, their attack roll made at the end of the charge, or their trip or bull rush combat maneuver attempt made after hitting the dragon.

#### Target Designation

**Prerequisite:** Warleader ((tactic) package).

**Effect:** The commander gains Marking Quarry as a bonus feat.

When using Marking Quarry, the commander’s mark is more potent than normal. Allies gain a +2 circumstance bonus on their first attack roll each round against the marked target. When triggered, the commander’s mark deals an additional +1d6 damage, +1d6 per 10 commander levels.

#### Troop Upkeep

*Through encouragement or harsh words, the commander pulls out every ounce of stamina their troops possess.*

At the start of the commander’s turn, each ally gains a number of temporary hit points equal to 1 + the commander’s practitioner modifier, +1 per 4 commander levels. These temporary hit points persist until lost or at the end of an ally’s turn if they are no longer under the effects of the commander’s *shouts* or *tactical coordination*.

#### Unrelenting March

While moving closer to an enemy, allies ignore up to 5 feet of difficult terrain each round, as though it were normal terrain (such as being able to take a 5-foot step into difficult terrain), plus an additional 5 feet of difficult terrain per 10 commander levels. Allies also roll twice and take the better result on saving throws and skill checks made to avoid having their movement impeded, such as to resist an entangle spell or safely travel across a slippery surface.

# Battlefield Specialties

A battlefield specialty represents the commander’s expertise, knowledge, and training at leading others through the hazards a given terrain represents. Each battlefield specialty may only be selected once.

The commander gains the benefits of their battlefield specialties as a constant effect. Any ally benefitting from the commander’s Warleader sphere effects also gains the commander’s battlefield specialties.

A battlefield specialty’s effects are not limited to the associated terrain and provide their benefits regardless of the battlefield (although some of their benefits may not be relevant without the terrain’s normal features present).

**Terrain Skill Bonus:** Each battlefield specialty grants a circumstance bonus to a skill equal to the commander’s practitioner modifier. This skill bonus is often related to navigating hazards common to that terrain. Other abilities and effects may reference a battlefield specialty’s terrain skill bonus.

If the commander would possess multiple battlefield specialties with the same terrain skill bonus, instead of adding the terrain skill bonus twice, the terrain skill bonus increases by an additional +1 per 3 commander levels they possess.

**Terrains and Weather Effects:** Certain battlefield specialties reference weather effects and the Weather sphere’s severities. If the Weather sphere and its rules are not in use, instead use the relevant weather rules.

**Example:** A commander with a desert battlefield specialty provides protections against heat exhaustion and fire damage, which is relevant to combat in desert terrains, but these effects are also relevant in sweltering jungles or magmatic caves. By contrast, a commander with the water battlefield specialty provides its benefits despite the lack of water to do combat in.

#### Cold

*Across wintry fields to the tops of the coldest of glaciers, the wintered soldiers brace against all.*

This battlefield specialty provides the following effects:

- **Terrain Skill Bonus:** Acrobatics. In addition, you roll twice and take the better result on Acrobatics checks made to move through slippery terrain, including ice or effects such as the *grease* spell.
- You are immune to nonlethal cold damage from cold weather (cold severity 4 and under).
- You can move across slippery terrain (such as ice or oil) at full speed and without penalty. In addition, you treat the penalties associated with moving through or fighting in snow, or heavy snow, as 1 step less severe (regular snow incurring no penalty, and heavy snow being treated as regular snow for its movement and other associated penalties).
- Whenever you move at least half your land speed, you can “slide” an additional 5 feet at the end of your movement or 10 feet if you move your full land speed. Sliding this way provokes attacks of opportunity, but any attack of opportunity made against this movement is rolled twice, taking the worse result.

See *PRPG Core Rulebook*, Cold Dangers and Rain, Snow, Sleet, and Hail for more information.

#### Desert

*Through arid valleys and over sandy dunes, soldiers move with the sands themselves.*

This battlefield specialty provides the following effects:

- **Terrain Skill Bonus:** Survival. In addition, you add this bonus as a bonus to the DC of Survival checks made to track you.
- You are immune to nonlethal fire damage from hot weather (heat severity 4 and under) and nonlethal damage caused by sandstorms.
- You halve any penalties to Perception caused by distance and ignore Perception penalties caused by environmental conditions, such as fog, rain, and sandstorms (including similar magical effects).
- When moving downhill, you gain a +10 circumstance bonus to your land speed, +5 feet per 5 commander levels. Any round you benefit from this additional movement speed you gain a +2 circumstance bonus on attack rolls.

See *PRPG Core Rulebook*, Desert Terrain and Heat Dangers for more information.

#### Forest

*Beneath covered boughs and across knotted roots, soldiers step between the silence.*

This battlefield specialty provides the following effects:

- **Terrain Skill Bonus:** Climb. In addition, you may climb one-handed.
- You gain the evasion ability when adjacent to or in the same square as an area of difficult terrain or object suitable to provide cover (this includes natural features such as foliage, trees, and natural stone formations, but also manufactured features such as palisades, window openings and hatches, and so on). At 10th level, you instead gain improved evasion.
- You treat the penalties associated with moving through or fighting in undergrowth as 1 step less severe (undergrowth incurring no penalty, and heavy undergrowth being treated as undergrowth for its movement and other associated penalties).
- You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to damage rolls made during a surprise round or against a flat-footed target, +1 per 10 commander levels.

See *PRPG Core Rulebook*, Forest Terrain for more information.

#### Mountain

*Scaling across rocky terrain, up sheer cliffs, and down narrow canyons, soldiers claim the high ground or stand guarded from below.*

This battlefield specialty provides the following effects:

- **Terrain Skill Bonus:** Climb. In addition, whenever you fall adjacent to a cliff, ledge, or climbable surface, as an immediate action you can make a Climb check to cling to the ledge (remaining one space below where you fell). The Climb check DC is equal to the surface’s Climb DC +10.
- You are always acclimated to high altitude and immune to the negative effects of high altitude.
- You can travel up a steep slope without spending additional movement and always succeed on Acrobatics checks made when running or charging down a steep slope. You also gain a +2 competence bonus to your CMD against bull rush, reposition, and trip combat maneuver attempts, increasing by +1 per 5 commander levels.
- You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your AC against ranged attacks made from a higher or lower elevation (at least 10 feet from your current elevation), +1 per 10 commander levels.

See *PRPG Core Rulebook*, Hill Terrain and Mountain Terrain for more information.

#### Plains

*Across tranquil farms and windswept fields, soldiers hold on to what is dear.*

This battlefield specialty provides the following effects:

- **Terrain Skill Bonus:** Survival. In addition, you can always take 10 on Survival checks.
- You halve the penalties for ranged attacks made due to high wind, and can make ranged attacks in high wind even if it would be impossible, instead suffering a -8 penalty to the attack roll. At 10th level, you now ignore all penalties, and only suffer a -4 penalty on attack rolls when it would be impossible.
- You can move over or across a single square of difficult terrain each round without spending additional movement (this effect also allows you to take a 5-foot step to move into difficult terrain). This also applies to areas which would require you to spend 2 squares of movement to move across, such as when moving over a mid height obstacle (fences, hedgerows, low walls, and so on) or when leaving a ditch or trench. If you could already ignore one or more squares of difficult terrain, this effect stacks.
- If you have not moved from your space since your previous turn, you increase your reach by +5 feet (or an additional +10 feet if wielding a reach weapon). You retain this increased reach until you move from your space. Movement granted by a commander class feature (such as an enhanced tactic) does not cause you to lose this increased reach.

See *PRPG Core Rulebook*, Plains Terrain for more information.

#### Swamp

*Squelching muck, pools and streams, soldiers make the best of being stuck in the mud.*

This battlefield specialty provides the following effects:

- **Terrain Skill Bonus:** Escape Artist. You can make Escape Artist checks 1 step faster when escaping from a grapple, net, or entangling spells (such as *entangle* or *control plants*).
- You can move through shallow and deep standing water or bogs as 1 step less severe (regular standing water incurring no penalty, and deep standing water being treated as regular standing water for its movement and other associated penalties).
- You roll twice and take the better result on saving throws made against the onset of a disease and poison. This does not apply to saving throws made against a disease or poison once afflicted (such as continued saving throws to resist). At 10th level, you roll twice on all saving throws made against disease and poison.
- You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to damage rolls against creatures suffering from an AC penalty, such as the entangled condition, +1 per 10 commander levels. This bonus does not apply against self-inflicted AC penalties, such as Berserker sphere’s *berserking* sphere ability.

See *PRPG Core Rulebook*, Marsh Terrain for more information.

#### Urban

*From the streets and roads, upwards to the rooftops or down into the sewers.*

This battlefield specialty provides the following effects:

- **Terrain Skill Bonus:** Stealth. In addition, you can always take 10 on Stealth checks.
- You can move through allied occupied squares or crowds without penalty, and can share your space with up to one other ally without penalty, +1 additional ally per 5 commander levels. This also allows you to charge through occupied allied squares.
- When adjacent to a wall or another ally, you gain uncanny dodge, as the rogue class feature with an effective level equal to the commander’s level. At 10th level, if you already possess uncanny dodge, this instead grants improved uncanny dodge.
- Whenever you benefit from cover, you retain cover’s bonus to AC and Reflex saving throws until the start of your next turn (but not any other benefit of cover, such as preventing attacks of opportunity or not being targeted due to full cover).

#### Underground

*Dark caverns and twisted narrow tunnels echo with footsteps.*

This battlefield specialty provides the following effects:

- **Terrain Skill Bonus:** Perception. You roll twice and take the better result on Perception checks to notice natural hazards, detect secret doors or passageways, or to locate traps.
- You gain low-light vision. If you already possess low-light vision, you instead triple the visibility of light sources (from two-times to three-times).
- While blind or otherwise unable to see (such as when in darkness without darkvision), you can move your full speed without making an Acrobatics check and halve the penalties for being blinded. At 10th level, you no longer suffer penalties while being blinded (but are still unable to see, and fail all checks or activities that rely on vision, and enemies still benefit from total concealment).
- You roll twice and take the better result on percentile rolls made against miss chance granted by concealment (including darkness, fog and mist, etc.). At 10th level, you roll twice against all sources of miss chance, not just concealment.

#### Water

*On the shores of placid lakes, over rapid rivers, and across the oceans and into their depths.*

This battlefield specialty provides the following effects:

- **Terrain Skill Bonus:** Swim. This bonus is doubled when making a Swim check to avoid being swept away. In addition, you can always take 10 on Swim checks.
- While underwater, you double the distance you can see and take no penalties when fighting with an unsuitable weapon (such as using a slashing or bludgeoning weapon). If you become off balance, you do not lose your Dexterity bonus to AC (but enemies still gain a bonus on attack rolls against you).
- While not in water, you ignore cover and improved cover granted to creatures in or at the surface of water. If a creature is fully submerged and would have total cover, you instead treat the creature as having just cover.
- You do not reduce the time you can hold your breath when taking a standard or full-round action, and can choose to begin holding your breath as an immediate action (such as in response to a hostile inhaled effect to avoid exposure).

See *PRPG Core Rulebook*, Aquatic Terrain and Suffocation for more information.

# Logistic Specialties

A logistics specialty represents the commander’s ability to coordinate or request resources and aid through their various contacts, or to lead their allies from battlefield to battlefield. This may take the form of supplies procured from an armory the commander has a good rapport with, to acquiring the temporary aid of the commander’s former brothers-in-arms.

A logistics specialty with the [plan] tag is treated as and may be readied as a [plan] talent. Each [plan] logistics specialty the commander possess counts towards the total number of plans the commander may prepare.

Unless otherwise stated, a logistic specialty may only be selected once.

#### Call in a Specialist [plan]

The commander leverages their vast network of contacts and connections to temporarily hire the services of a “**specialist**”.

When the commander reveals this plan, the specialist arrives in 24 hours, minus 1 hour per commander level (minimum 1 hour). Each specialist assists the commander and their allies by providing specific services, as noted in their entries, and will accompany the commander in their travels as a noncombatant, avoiding danger where possible (unless otherwise stated, certain specialists may act as combatants).

The commander can reveal this plan no more than once per week, and calling in a new specialist dismisses the previous specialist.

**Special:** If the commander possesses the call in a specialist logistics specialty from multiple sources, the commander’s effective class level for this logistics specialty stacks and the commander may recruit specialists from either source, but the commander does not gain the ability to have more specialists active at the same time.

##### About Specialists

Each specialist is a specific NPC that offers services, similar to a Leadership sphere (follower) talent, but each more powerful and offering more variety in their services. The commander may replace a specific specialist in 1 month’s time, such as when a specialist dies or if the commander chooses to replace that specialist.

A specialist is typically a humanoid race NPC with a class level equal to the commander’s class level -3, unless otherwise specified.

**Specialist Services:** A specialist offers their “**services**”, discrete and specific benefits or effects based on their specialist type. Services are most often in the form of class features or spellcasting, but also may be actions such as scouting or information gathering. A specialist does not offer all of the abilities at their disposal, such as a healer specialist cleric providing the services of a healer, not the full range of spellcasting they otherwise have at their disposal except as necessary to protect themselves, nor would the healer specialist cleric craft magic items on the commander’s behalf unless they were for healing. If a specialist would provide services that require gold, such as crafting, the commander must supply the specialist with all required costs and resources. Specialists are noncombatants unless otherwise specified.

**Building Specialists:** For each specialist, either the commander or the GM should build an NPC, similar to building a Leadership feat cohort. For example, an information specialist would select a conspiracy as a mastermind.

The following specialist types and their services are available to the commander:

##### Equipment Specialist

**Class:** Alchemist or Blacksmith.

**Services:** Alchemist’s alchemy (but only formulae that target equipment and objects) or Blacksmith’s maintenance and reforge. The specialist may also use any features or abilities that modify or improve equipment and objects.

In addition, the specialist can craft using their item creation feats.

##### Information Specialist

**Class:** Agent or Mastermind.

**Services:** Agent or mastermind’s web of secrets (based on their conspiracy). The specialist may also use any features or abilities that gather information.

Through the specialist’s own unique connections, the specialist can also provide the commander with detailed maps of a local town or city, including hidden passages and sewer entrances, business and guild halls (both legal and illegal), and other points of interest.

In addition, the specialist can study either a single location in a city (such as a building, city block, or similar specific area) or individual. After 1+1d4 days, the specialist provides detailed information. For a location, this includes traffic, demographics, notable or dangerous individuals, and other points of interest. For an individual, this includes the individual’s friends and contacts, significant abilities (martial prowess, spellcasting, etc.), possessions of note or value, and addictions, habits, minor motivations, and social weaknesses.

##### Medical Specialist

**Class:** Cleric or Scholar.

**Services:** The specialist uses their casting or class features (such as channel energy, medical training, spellcasting, Alchemy sphere *formulae* and so on) to treat wounds and remove conditions. The specialist must be supplied with any expensive material components or reagents.

In addition, once per day, the specialist may perform an extended ritual taking 1 hour. This ritual restores a dead creature back to life, provided a majority of the remains are present and the creature has been dead for less than 1 day per commander level. Resurrecting a creature this way costs 1,000 gp.

##### Scouting Specialist

**Class:** Courser or Ranger.

**Services:** Courser’s forage or ranger’s spells and the ability to share favored terrain bonuses (shared at half its normal bonus). The specialist may also use any features or abilities that assist in traveling or mitigating weather (such as Navigation acclimations).

Through the specialist’s own prior travels, the specialist can provide the commander with detailed maps of local wilderness, including pathways and hazards, dungeons and ruins, bestial lairs and dens, and other points of interest. The specialist maps up to 1 square mile each day before producing a map with suitable information. This map also includes information about species mapped in the area, including their territory or dens.

Alternatively, the specialist can provide information on a single creature. After 1+1d4 days, the specialist provides detailed information on that creature. This includes the creature’s current condition, any weaknesses or prior injuries, its supernatural or other abilities, and its habits and daily routine (where it goes and why, if it is social, etc.).

**Author’s Note - Other Specialists:** The specialist types above are meant to be a general, wide net of the types of connections a commander would have to call upon. Subject to GM discretion, a specialist may be a different class, provided they offer substantially the same services.

#### Faction Connections

The commander gains the Faction sphere (*Spheres of Guile*) as a bonus sphere plus 1 additional Faction talent.

#### Leadership Connections

The commander gains the Leadership sphere as a bonus sphere plus 1 additional Leadership talent.

#### Mercantile Connections [plan]

*The commander always knows the best places to find their supplies.*

The commander reduces the price they pay for items by 5%, increased to 10% for nonmagical items. This does not reduce the price of services or materials for crafting, only finished goods.

In addition, the commander may prepare this logistic specialty as a plan. When the commander reveals this plan, a merchant caravan arrives at the commander’s location in 24 hours, minus 1 hour per commander level (to a minimum of 1 hour) and remains for up to 24 hours. The merchant caravan will travel to any location, regardless of distance or remoteness, including dangerous locations such as dungeons or volcanoes, but not to areas with restricted travel (such as an embargoed city, a travel-restricted demiplane, etc.). The commander may only reveal this plan once per week.

Each merchant caravan is treated as a settlement with a purchase value of 1000 gp per commander level, and a purchase limit of 2000 gp per commander level. A merchant caravan’s magic item availability is equivalent to a large city. See *PRPG Core Rulebook*, Settlements in Play **Table 7-36** and **7-37** for more details.

At 13th level, the merchant caravan’s magic item availability improves to that of a metropolis, and doubles the number of medium and major magic items available. In addition, the merchant’s caravan can source and make available rare and unusual consumables, equipment, and other paraphernalia, including “regionally unique” specialties (subject to GM discretion).

At 19th level, the merchant caravan has access to planar trade routes and no longer has a purchase value or purchase limit, able to sell any items and any number of items. In addition, the merchant caravan always finds the means to arrive, even to areas with restricted travel.

**Note - Settlement Rules:** This logistics specialty uses the settlement rules for purchase value, purchase limit, and item availability. GMs should treat the merchant caravan called by this logistic specialty as being the same as a large marketplace to buy and sell goods based on other settlements in the game. If not using settlement statistics to determine purchase value and purchase limits, or magic item availability, treat the merchant caravan as an exotic, bountiful marketplace.

#### Overland March [plan]

The commander and allies traveling with the commander (the “**commander’s march**”) double their overland movement speed. When making a forced march, the commander’s march does not need to make Constitution checks against fatigue until after 16 hours of forced marching (effectively allowing the commander’s march to travel overland for up to 24 hours without making Constitution checks). Once a Constitution check would be required, the DC is based on the total number of hours the commander’s march spent forced marching.

See *PRPG Core Rulebook*, Overland Movement for details. For the purposes of this ability, the commander’s march assumes all creatures traveling as a group use the slowest overland travel speed of their group (so as to not leave an individual behind).

At 13th level, the commander can prepare this logistic specialty as a plan. When the commander reveals this plan, the commander immediately becomes aware of a passageway, whether it is a secret tunnel, ancient highway, planar rift, or other place, that is within 8 hours of travel for the commander’s march. The commander’s march may travel through this passageway to immediately appear within 1 day’s overland travel to their destination (or reasonably close to it, subject to GM discretion).

The passageways the commander utilizes with this plan are shifting, unreliable, or unsteady, and only last for 48 hours after the commander reveals this plan. After this time, the passageway disappears, becomes unpassable, or is otherwise no longer accessible.

The commander may only reveal this plan once per week.

At 19th level, the passageway is within 1 hour of overland travel for the commander’s march, and the commander’s march appears within 1 hour of overland travel to their destination.

The commander may now reveal this plan once per day (although revealing this plan again causes a previous passageway to become inert).

**Example:** During overland travel, the commander and their allies can move up to 4 times their normal overland travel distance (including 16 hours of forced march at twice their normal speed) before making Constitution checks against fatigue (DC 34, equal to 10 + 2 per hour spent forced marching).

#### Requisition [plan]

*Whether by arranging to have things delivered to a predetermined location or contacting preferred merchants and vendors, the commander can requisition additional resources, provisions, and tools for themselves and their allies.*

When this plan is revealed, the commander selects one of the requisition options detailed below, with the chosen requisition’s benefits or effects arriving 15 minutes after this plan is revealed. The commander may only reveal this plan once per day, and may never benefit from the same requisition option more than once in the same day.

**Special:** The commander may select this logistics specialty multiple times; if they do, the commander may now reveal this plan an additional time each day, provided that they use this plan to select different requisitions.

##### Requisition Maintenance

*The commander arranges for emergency field maintenance and improvements to their and their allies’ equipment.*

The commander designates any number of equipment, removing the broken condition and restoring a number of hit points equal to 1d6 + the commander’s practitioner modifier. The commander cannot restore destroyed equipment this way.

In addition to the repairs, the commander may further improve their or their allies’ equipment. The commander gains a number of maintenance points equal to 1 per odd commander level, which may be expended for temporary improvements (listed below). Maintenance points not spent after revealing this plan are lost. Any improvements granted this way last for 24 hours. A single piece of equipment may only benefit from each improvement once (such as increasing its enhancement bonus by 1, granting it a special property, and making it treated as a second material, but not increasing its enhancement bonus twice or granting it two special properties).

**Improvements**

- **Increased Enhancement (1 point):** The commander improves the enhancement bonus of a single weapon, armor, or shield by +1. This improvement may also be applied to implements, but only if that implement already possessed an enhancement bonus. At 15th level, this improvement may increase the enhancement bonus of that equipment up to +6.
- **Special Material (1 point):** The commander temporarily coats a single weapon, armor, or shield with an alloying blanche. The commander chooses from: adamantine, alchemical silver, cold iron, mithral, and darkwood.

  The equipment is treated as both its original material and the chosen material for all purposes. If the new material would change the item’s statistics (such as damage, weight, armor check penalty, spell failure, and so on), the more beneficial of the two material’s properties are used. The equipment must have been able to be originally crafted from the selected material (such as being unable to choose adamantine for a quarterstaff).
- **Special Property (1+ points):** The commander chooses a single special weapon, armor, or shield property, granting it to a single piece of equipment. A special property whose enhancement value is +1 costs 1 point, +2 costs 3 points, and +3 costs 5 points. At 15th level, the maintenance point cost of any special property applied this way is reduced by 1 (to a minimum of 1; a +1 property still costs 1, but now +2 costs 2 and +3 costs 4).

##### Requisition Mounts

*Calling in favors from small stables or local lords, the commander is never without a ride.*

The commander gains temporary access to mounts for themselves and any number of their allies. Mounts procured this way may be any animal capable of carrying a rider that is well-equipped to travel through local terrain (such as horses in plains, camels in a desert, mammoths in a tundra, dolphins to cross oceans, hippogriffs to fly across deep valleys, and so on). Any mount procured this way has up to 1 Hit Die per odd commander level (such as procuring 4 Hit Die mounts at commander level 7).

The commander may continue to reveal this plan to retain access to mounts requisitioned this way. Mounts obtained from this requisition option are well marked as belonging to someone else and will not be accepted by traders or other groups, as they recognize these mounts will escape or refuse to cooperate.

These mounts are combat trained and will assist their respective rider to the best of their ability, but will refuse obviously harmful and suicidal orders. These mounts will also refuse to travel to unusually dangerous or unsuitable environments (such as dungeons or volcanoes, hostile cities, etc.) unless they are well suited to traveling through that environment.

At 15th level, mounts provided through this requisition have a simple aligned or elemental template (celestial, fiendish, anarchic, entropic, aerial, aqueous, cthonic, or fiery). At GM discretion, other “+0 or +1” CR adjustment templates may be appropriate (such as first world, if requisitioning mounts to travel through fey planes).

##### Requisition Provisions

*The commander produces food and drink, whether foraged from their surroundings, acquired from a recent town, or liberated from a recently defeated enemy warband.*

The commander produces a meal suitable for 1 creature per commander level. The number of creatures the commander may feed doubles at 13th level, and every 6 levels thereafter (2 creatures per commander level at 13th, 4 creatures per commander level at 19th, and so on).

Any creature that spends 10 minutes to eat the meal gains the benefits of a *heroes’ feast*, treating their commander level as their caster level. The morale bonus to attack rolls and Will saving throws granted by the meal increases by an additional +1 at 13th level and every 6 levels thereafter. Any parts of the meal not consumed within 1 hour is wasted (and cannot be preserved by any means).

# Favored Class Bonuses

A commander of any race can choose from the following alternate favored class bonuses:

- +1/3 to the commander’s decorum bonus (but not the saving throw DC increase).
- Gain +1/6 of an enhanced tactic.
- Gain +1/8 of a battlefield specialty.
- Your lingering commands lasts +1/4 additional rounds.

# Class Equipment

The following magical items are especially appropriate for commanders.

## All-Terrain Armoire

**Aura** faint Nature and Protection; **CL** 6th
**Slot** none; **Price** 20,000 gp; **Weight** 300 lbs.

This heavy, full-size wooden armoire is made of thick, durable wood that seems almost impervious to all temperature changes and can protect the contents within. While a creature with the battlefield specialist class feature is in one of their specialized terrains, that creature can use this armoire to outfit any number of allies over the course of ten minutes with special clothing appropriate to that terrain. This grants all such creatures a +5 circumstance bonus to Survival checks while in that terrain.

Twice per day, as a standard action, a commander can call out specialized instructions to grant the benefits of another battlefield specialist terrain they know for a number of rounds equal to the higher of their Intelligence or Charisma modifiers. For example, a commander could use this armoire to temporarily grant the benefits of being in swampy terrain while in an urban environment.

**Construction Requirements**
Craft Apparatus, Craft Marvelous Item, Nature sphere, Protection sphere, creator must have the battlefield specialist ability; **Cost** 10,000 gp

## Amplifying Horn

**Aura** moderate War; **CL** 7th
**Slot** none; **Price** 16,000 gp; **Weight** 3 lbs.

This silvery horn excels at amplifying the user’s voice to let them be heard across the battlefield. When used by a creature with the lingering commands ability, this horn allows creatures benefiting from the lingering commands to leave the normal radius of a tactic and continue to receive its benefits until the lingering commands wear off (as long as they remain within line of sight to the commander).

**Construction Requirements**
Craft Apparatus, War sphere (Lingering Resentment), creator must have the lingering commands ability; **Cost** 8,000 gp

## Tactics Manual

**Aura** faint War; **CL** 5th
**Slot** none; **Price** 15,500 gp; **Weight** 4 lbs.

This thick, metal-bound book contains a variety of tactics and strategies covering warfare in countless situations and circumstances, from individual combat to battles with tens of thousands of soldiers on each side. Although the author appears to view war as ultimately futile, carrying this tome grants a creature with the enhanced tactics class feature an additional enhanced tactic, chosen when the manual is written. In addition, twice per day, a creature with the enhanced tactics class feature can switch enhanced tactics as a free action twice per round instead of once per round. A creature can only benefit from one tactics manual at a time and must spend eight hours reading a different manual to change the one they receive benefits from.

**Construction Requirements**
Craft Apparatus, War sphere (Tactical Momentum (momentum)), creator must know the enhanced tactic added to this item; **Cost** 7,750 gp
